## Answer
To upload a local file to Azure Blob Storage using the Python SDK, you can use the `BlobClient` class along with its `upload_blob` method. You can instantiate the `BlobClient` using a connection string or a storage URL with credentials, open your local file in binary read mode (`"rb"`), and then call `upload_blob(data)`. 

Here is an example using a connection string:

```python
from azure.storage.blob import BlobClient

blob = BlobClient.from_connection_string(conn_str="<connection_string>", container_name="mycontainer", blob_name="my_blob")

with open("./SampleSource.txt", "rb") as data:
    blob.upload_blob(data)
```

# Security triage: demo_app
## Summary
The codebase contains several high-severity security vulnerabilities, including command injection and insecure deserialisation in web handlers. Finding F5 should be fixed first because it allows unauthenticated remote code execution via direct shell command concatenation.

## Findings
| ID | Rule | Location | Verdict | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | py-weak-hash | app/cache.py:9 | false positive | MD5 is used solely to derive a cache bucket key from a URL, not for cryptographic verification or passwords. | Keep as-is or switch to sha256 for non-crypto uniqueness. |
| F2 | py-pickle-load | app/cache.py:14 | likely | `pickle.loads` deserialises session cookies; exploitable if an attacker can forge or tamper with the session cookie value. |

## Answer
The 5 genres with the most tracks are Rock (1,297 tracks), Latin (579 tracks), Metal (374 tracks), Alternative & Punk (332 tracks), and Jazz (130 tracks).

| Genre | TrackCount |
|---|---|
| Rock | 1297 |

## SQL used
```sql
SELECT g.Name AS Genre, COUNT(t.TrackId) AS TrackCount
FROM Genre g
JOIN Track t ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY TrackCount DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
